Ms. Kumari Rashmi, A.P.P  -----
02/14.08.2024 Heard learned counsel for the parties.
2.
The petitioners apprehending their arrest in connection with the case registered under Sections 406/420/506/34 IPC and Section 27 of the Arms Act have prayed for grant of anticipatory bail.
3. Learned Sr. counsel for the petitioners submits that the petitioners have been falsely implicated in this case and have not committed any offence as alleged in the F.I.R.
The entire story made out by the informant in the FIR is false and concocted.

As per the allegation, the petitioner and few other co- accused persons threatened the informant on gun point not to purchase the land being sold by co-accused Sweta Chaubey and her agnate-Sarvesh Chaubey.
Though the petitioners have the criminal antecedent, however, so far as the present case is concerned, they have been implicated without any cogent evidence.
They also undertake to co-operate in the ongoing investigation.

Hence,
they may be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

4. Learned A.P.P while opposing the petitioners' prayer for anticipatory bail, submits that the petitioners have criminal antecedent and hence they may not be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.
5. Considering the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to enlarge the petitioners on anticipatory bail.
Accordingly, the above named petitioners are directed to surrender before the concerned Court below within a period of three weeks.
If they surrender before the Court Mangal Murti Tiwari vs The State Of Jharkhand .....
